aspect: EXAMPLE - eighty hours at Sal Airport, then Senegal
description: The Institute for Human Rights and Development in Africa filed a case before the ECOWAS Court of Justice against Cabo Verde on behalf of five Nigerian travellers, alleging that despite valid travel documents, return tickets, accommodation and sufficient funds they were singled out at Sal Airport, detained over 80 hours and deported to Senegal in April 2025.
energy_note: Everything in order, and eighty hours in a room.

aspect: EXAMPLE - watchlisted for a social media post
description: Three Nigerians denied entry at OR Tambo in April 2026 said they were unlawfully detained despite valid visas, and that a phone was seized. Nigeria's diaspora commission said one had been flagged for previously making insulting remarks about the South African government online, placing him on a watchlist.
energy_note: Refused entry over an old post about the government.

aspect: ECOWAS free movement is a right with a desk in front of it
description: Nigerians hold a regional free-movement entitlement that is nonetheless administered by individual officers at individual airports, which is why a case had to be filed to establish it.
energy_note: A right that required a court to notice.

aspect: The cost of a refusal at the far end
description: Return flight, the nights held, the purpose of the trip lost, and in several cases the phone or documents retained. None of it is compensated.
energy_note: Paid for the trip, then paid to come back.
